evals.name: process-heat-trough
evals.prompt: Size a small parabolic trough for 150 °C process heat at a dairy near Almería. We already buy 35 mm evacuated receiver tubes with 65 mm glass. Rows can be 60 m long. Give me a design file I can open in Linefocus and tell me the yearly yield.
evals.expected_output: A .linefocus.json trough with a 35 mm absorber in a 65 mm envelope at Almería, verified, with design-point efficiency, intercept factor, acceptance and a yearly yield stated with its weather caveat.
assertions: Produced a file that the Linefocus loader (parseDesign) accepts
collector.type is "trough" and receiver.absorberDiameter is 0.035 with envelope.outerDiameter 0.065
verify.mjs reports no errors and the intercept factor is at least 0.9
The answer states the optical efficiency with its reference (aperture, with cos θ)
The answer says the yearly figure is a clear-sky upper bound, or uses an EPW file

evals.name: trough-versus-lfr
evals.prompt: For a site at Upington, South Africa, compare a EuroTrough-class parabolic trough with a 16-row linear Fresnel field on yearly energy per square metre of mirror. Which collects more, and by how much?
evals.expected_output: Two design files at Upington, both verified, compared with verify.mjs on yearly energy per m² of aperture, with the difference and an explanation (cosine and end losses for the LFR).
assertions: Produced two .linefocus.json files, one trough and one fresnel, both at latitude about −28.4
Both use the same sunshape and weather source
Ran verify.mjs on both files together and reported the comparison table
Stated the yearly kWh/m² of each and which is larger
Explained the difference in terms of cosine loss, incidence angle or end losses rather than design-point efficiency alone

evals.name: best-receiver-height
evals.prompt: I have a linear Fresnel design (the Linefocus default). What receiver height gives the best optical efficiency at the design point, and is the improvement real?
evals.expected_output: An optimise.mjs run on collector.receiverHeight with the efficiency objective, reporting the best height, the confirmed gain and the sampling noise, and an updated file only if the gain is real.
assertions: Ran optimise.mjs with --objective efficiency and --vary collector.receiverHeight
Reported the best receiver height between 5 and 9 m
Reported the confirmed gain alongside the sampling noise
Wrote an optimised file only if the tool reported a gain beyond the noise, and verified it
